item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 280508
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Mon Jul 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on recently
downgraded Tropical Storm Fausto, located in the Central Pacific
several hundred miles east-northeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on
Hurricane Genevieve, located several hundred miles southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.description:

000

BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
200 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026
 
...GENEVIEVE REMAINS A POWERFUL MAJOR HURRICANE WELL AWAY FROM
LAND...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.5N 115.4W
ABOUT 515 MI...830 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...140 MPH...220 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...943 MB...27.85 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Genevieve was
located near latitude 17.5 North, longitude 115.4 West. Genevieve is
moving toward the northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h).  A motion toward 
the west-northwest or northwest is expected during the next few 
days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 140 mph (220 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Genevieve is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  Steady weakening is forecast over the next 
several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles
(280 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 943 mb (27.85 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the
southwestern coast of Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula.
These swells are likely to persist for a few more days, and could
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026 
022 
WTPZ42 KNHC 280834
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
200 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026
 
Genevieve remains a powerful major hurricane, but it is gradually 
losing strength.  Although the cyclone is maintaining a distinct 15 
n mi diameter eye, deep convection in the eyewall has become a 
little less symmetric with some dry slots occasionally evident in 
the northwestern quadrant.  The 06Z satellite intensity estimates 
range from 105 to 120 kt, and based on that data, the initial 
intensity is nudged downward to 120 kt, but this could be a little 
generous.  A Synthetic Aperture Radar pass did hint at the 
possibility of a secondary eyewall beginning to form, but 
unfortunately, there have not been any recent microwave images to 
confirm that.  An ASCAT pass from around 04Z was helpful in updating 
the initial wind radii.
 
The hurricane continues to move northwestward at about 9 kt.  The
track forecast philosophy appears straightforward.  A mid-level
ridge centered over the southwestern U.S. is expected to expand
westward over the next few days, and that should cause Genevieve to
move at a faster pace to the west-northwest later this week and into
the weekend.  The models are in fairly good agreement, and the NHC
forecast lies near the fast side of the guidance envelope, placing 
greater weight on the HCCA and Google DeepMind solutions.
 
Although there could be some fluctuations in Genevieve's strength
in the short term due to the potential of an eyewall replacement
cycle, weakening should be the primary theme during the remainder
of the week due to progressively cooler waters and drier air along
the forecast track.  The NHC intensity forecast lies near the
middle of the guidance envelope, and calls for Genevieve to fall
below hurricane strength in a few days and become post-tropical
this weekend.
